correctness.rationale: The unit simplex tight-frame map identifies squared directional residuals with any zero-sum z of fixed norm S=(n+1)/n. One-step orthogonal projection loses exactly the sampled maximum z_i^2. When m=n+1 odd, the nonstandard inequality D=sum_{i<j}|z_i^2-z_j^2| >= S follows from sorted magnitudes: one sign carries at most (m-1)/2 positions but half the absolute mass, forcing the large-magnitude gap constraint; summation by parts has coefficients c_i=(i-1)(m-i)>=(m-1)h_i/2. The two-sample expected maximum is S/m+D/[m(m-1)]; equality is attained by opposite pairs ±a plus one zero, with every β≥2 sample meeting a nonzero. Even m has balanced ±a and constant squares, giving 1/n for all β. β=1 follows by tightness. Independently checked 60,000 bounded random integer zero-sum vectors in odd cardinalities and inspected exact-grid source checker; analytic lemma, not bounded checking, proves all dimensions.
residual_risks: Performance is conditional one-step worst-case decrease; multistep equality is NOT inferred.
